business_scope.primary_industry_name: Wholesale Remarketing of Secondhand Hydraulic Earthmovers and Rollers

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Egypt (national unitary jurisdiction; no tax autonomy at sub-state level)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid Civil Law (French-model codes) with Islamic Sharia as the principal source of legislation pursuant to Article 2 of the Egyptian Constitution
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Egypt-United States Trade and Investment Framework Agreement (1999)
COMESA Treaty member state; Arab League Unified Agreement for the Investment of Arab Capital
Over 50 double-taxation avoidance agreements in force, including with the UK, the Netherlands, France, Germany, China, Saudi Arabia and the UAE

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing, as amended by Law No. 36 of 2014 and Law No. 154 of 2019; Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended, and the new Companies Law No. 72 of 2023 (mandatory beneficial ownership disclosure); GAFI implementing regulations on the Register of Ultimate Beneficial Owners; Central Bank of Egypt Egyptian Money Laundry Combat Unit (EMLCU) customer due diligence directives; FATF mutual evaluation follow-up requirements.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of each foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial registry or corporate registry in the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (Egypt is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention of 1961; the document must be legalized by the competent Egyptian embassy or consulate abroad and countersigned by the Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the foreign parent company's Memorandum and Articles of Association
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or corporate registry of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (Hague Apostille not recognized by Egypt)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate board resolution authorizing the incorporation of the Egyptian LLC and designating the ultimate beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign parent company's board secretary or notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (Hague Apostille not recognized by Egypt)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport copy and proof of residential address of each non-Egyptian individual shareholder and director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority or police residence registry of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (for all non-Egyptian natural persons)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming source of funds for the intended paid-in capital
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Due diligence bank or correspondent bank of the foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization or, where issued by an Egyptian bank, notarized Arabic certified translation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, signatories and ultimate beneficial owners against the UN Security Council consolidated list, the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals list, the EU and UK consolidated sanctions lists, the Arab League counter-terrorism list, and the Egyptian CBE/EMLCU domestic watchlists; mandatory PEP classification and enhanced due diligence under Article 4 of Law No. 80 of 2002 and CBE EMLCU directives; source-of-funds verification is required for capital remittances exceeding the statutory threshold; cash and wire transactions above USD 10,000 require EMLCU reporting; for the secondhand heavy machinery trading sector, cross-border sellers, end purchasers, freight forwarders and customs brokers are separately risk-rated under FATF-based enhanced due diligence standards.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) one-stop shop online platform (business.gov.eg / gafi.gov.eg) operating jointly with the Commercial Registry of the Ministry of Trade and Industry
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be entered in Arabic script in the Commercial Registry; a Latin-script phonetic transliteration or English commercial name may be registered as a secondary name only. The Arabic name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered corporate name, any reserved GAFI name, or any registered Egyptian trademark, and must not mislead the public as to the company's activity, legal form, size, or affiliation with the state or public sector.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, GAFI issues a written refusal identifying the conflicting name or prohibited token. Within 10 business days the legal representative may file a written administrative grievance with the GAFI Legal Affairs Department, attaching a trademark search certificate from the Egyptian Trademark Office where relevant. If the grievance is denied, an annulment action may be lodged with the Administrative Court of the Egyptian State Council within 30 days of notification. In parallel, the applicant may immediately re-submit a new distinctive Arabic name without prejudice to the pending appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as the sole registered address. Companies Law No. 72 of 2023 and GAFI one-stop shop practice require a physically leased or owned commercial premise in Egypt evidenced by a notarized lease agreement registered with the real-estate registry. A virtual administrative office may only supplement, not replace, the physical address. For a used heavy machinery trading LLC, a dedicated commercial office and a secure storage or inspection yard are expected by the Commercial Registry as evidence of commercial substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium-High; estimated 45% probability of an unannounced GAFI or Commercial Registry physical inspection within the first 12 months of incorporation for a goods-trading LLC; the likelihood increases to approximately 60% if the registered address is a shared, serviced, or mixed residential/commercial premise, or if the company's declared activity involves used equipment requiring customs and used-goods import verification.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law No. 149 of 2019, as amended by Law No. 185 of 2020, and its Executive Regulations (Cabinet Decree No. 96 of 2020); LLC formation and governance under Articles 249-286; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 (GAFI one-stop-shop procedures); Commercial Registration under Law No. 17 of 1999; Tax registration under Law No. 91 of 2005.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI), Companies Registration Department (One-Stop Shop), in coordination with the Commercial Registry Office of the Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association (filed electronically via GAFI-INC-02 through the GAFI Investment Services Portal), followed by Commercial Registry enrollment.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital under Law 149 of 2019; the capital is freely determined by the founders in the Memorandum of Association. The full cash tranche must be deposited into a temporary escrow bank account in the company's name with a licensed Egyptian bank prior to incorporation, and the bank deposit certificate must be attached to the incorporation file. In-kind contributions require a licensed accountant's valuation report.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the share capital provided in the Memorandum of Association be subscribed in full by the founding shareholders and the cash portion deposited to the Company's temporary escrow bank account with a licensed Egyptian bank. RESOLVED, that the registered office be fixed at [address], in [governorate], Arab Republic of Egypt, and the General Manager be authorized to register the office with GAFI, the Commercial Registry, and the Tax Authority. RESOLVED, that Mr. [Name] be appointed General Manager, Mr. [Name] Finance Director, and Mr. [Name] AML Compliance Officer, each authorized severally to open bank accounts, sign agreements, and execute trade documents. RESOLVED, that [Audit Firm] be appointed statutory auditor. RESOLVED, that management file for tax, social insurance, and import registrations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Trade Name Reservation and Activity Pre-Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop (Investment Services Portal at gafi.gov.eg or regional GAFI branches)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the integrated name reservation request in Arabic listing three alternative names and the precise activity code (ISIC 4659 - wholesale of used construction machinery). GAFI automatically cross-checks the Commercial Registry prohibited list and previously recorded trademarks. On approval, the name certificate is valid for 60 days and is a prerequisite to all subsequent filings.
required_dossiers: GAFI name reservation application (Arabic)
Passport or national ID of each founder and ultimate beneficial owner
Certified power of attorney if a corporate notarial agent files
Project activity description referencing the secondary activity of warehousing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file a written objection within 15 days; the GAFI grievance desk normally accepts revised alternatives in the same file without a second fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarization of the Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Legalization and Notarization Office (attached to the One-Stop Shop)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Arabic-language MoA/AoA using the GAFI standard template, stating the corporate name, business purpose, share capital, quota distribution, manager provisions, and registered office governorate. The founders or an attorney holding a certified power of attorney must appear in person or through their appointed representatives to acknowledge signatures before the GAFI notary. After statutory signature certification, the notarized instrument returns to the founders for the bank deposit step.
required_dossiers: GAFI standard template MoA/AoA (completed)
Name reservation certificate
Valid IDs or passports of all founders
Power of attorney files if externally signed
Declaration of no prior disqualification for founders (bankruptcy, criminal, tax fraud)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Only notary-flagged corrections are typically required; amend the flagged articles in the same visit via the marginal correction stamp, without a full re-filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Capital Deposit and Escrow Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any licensed Egyptian commercial bank (recommended: NBE or Banque Misr head-office branches familiar with GAFI forms)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary corporate escrow account in the exact intended company name, deposit the full called cash capital, and request the standardized GAFI bank deposit certificate. The bank verifies the beneficial ownership register and performs enhanced due diligence consistent with the designated medium-risk heavy-machinery trading profile. The certified deposit receipt is attached to the incorporation dossier; funds are locked until GAFI issues the certificate.
required_dossiers: Notarized MoA/AoA (from Step 2)
Name approval certificate
Passport or ID and residence proof of signatories
Bank KYC form with beneficial ownership declaration (Egypt EDD questionnaire)
Source of funds statement, including the supply agreement for used excavator inventory
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional wealth documentation, submit audited financial statements of the direct investors or a personal bank reference letter. If the bank rejects the file for PEP classification, an alternative licensed bank should be used and the GAFI helpdesk can mediate within five working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Filing with GAFI and Certificate Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Companies Registration Department (central One-Stop Shop at Cairo, Smart Village, or regional governorate branches)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the complete incorporation package electronically through the GAFI Investment Services Portal or at the One-Stop Shop counter. GAFI's review, including transcription of the MoA into the Commercial Registry and issuance of the company's corporate identification data card, normally takes five working days under the Law 149/2019 silence-is-consent rule. The corporate certificate enables the company to execute contracts and open accounts only after Step 6 registrations are made.
required_dossiers: Notarized MoA/AoA (Step 2 original)
Bank capital deposit certificate (Step 3)
Name approval certificate
Notarized lease contract or ownership deed of the registered office
GAFI-INC-02 application signed by managers
Receipt of the official fees (approx USD 150 total GAFI and registry duties)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For any formal query, GAFI sends an electronic notification with a 30-day correction window; if the statutory timeline is exceeded without a decision, a written complaint to the GAFI Grievance Committee under Investment Law Article 31 triggers a five-working-day mandatory reply.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registry Enrollment and Chamber of Commerce Dues
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registry Office at the competent governorate (Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade) and the Egyptian Federation of Chambers of Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The authorized manager appears to register the company in the Commercial Registry record and obtains the headroom to issue commercial invoices. The registrar verifies that GAFI issued the company's data card. Pay the local chamber subscription and applicable annual registry tax on the registered capital. The Commercial Registration booklet is the primary document for the Tax Authority and customs in subsequent steps.
required_dossiers: GAFI incorporation certificate
Tax card or GAFI-issued tax data
Manager's national ID and corporate ID
Registered office lease agreement with property tax receipt
Completed Commercial Registration form CR-01 (Arabic)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry demands a separate property tax clearance, obtain the local real-estate tax unit certificate confirming lawful occupancy; alternatively, a notarized short-term lease can be presented to restart the review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT, and Social Insurance Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA, Head Office) and the National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: GAFI's one-stop channels the commercial registration data to ETA. Confirm the electronic issuance of the tax identification number (TIN) on the ETA portal; if not automatically issued, file the registration form and attach the commercial booklet and lease. Register for VAT if turnover is expected to exceed EGP 500,000 per annum within 12 months; the used-machinery trade will be subject to reverse-charge import VAT and import duties settled through customs clearance. Register all employees and managers with NOSI on the unified payroll form and obtain the employer's insurance number.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registration booklet
Lease contract of the head office
GAFI incorporation certificate
ETA registration form (F-1/70) with the business purpose code 4659
NOSI employer registration form and opening pay list
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If ETA announces a late-filing penalty, file an administrative waiver citing registry delay; under Article 75 of Law 91/2005 the penalty is remissible when the delay is attributable to an official registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Importer Registration, GOEIC Used-Machinery Compliance, and Customs Code
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Organization for Export and Import Control (GOEIC) and the Egyptian Customs Authority (ECA) importer register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for inclusion in the importers' record and obtain the Importer Code. Since ISIC 4659 covers used hydraulic earthmovers, submit each consignment for a pre-shipment inspection certificate confirming year of manufacture, working condition, and absence of ODS or hazardous waste; the documents accompany the import declaration. Under current GOEIC directives, excavators older than 15 years require a separate investigation permission from the Ministry of Trade and Industry prior to shipment. This step can be run in parallel with Step 6.
required_dossiers: Commercial registration booklet and tax card
Importer code application (GOEIC form)
Pro-forma invoices and purchase contracts for each used excavator lot
Pre-shipment inspection certificate from an approved PSI company
Certificate of origin and proof of title for the second-hand machines
Ministry of Trade investigation decision for machines exceeding the age cutoff
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For refusal of used-machine import authorization, appeal to GOEIC's Complaint Committee with additional maintenance records and a full technical audit report; alternatively, opt for the Suez Canal Economic Zone regime where more flexible used-machinery import procedures apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Industrial Development Authority (IDA) - responsible only for factory licenses; for the pure wholesale trading of used construction machinery, no industrial or manufacturing license is issued by IDA. The only mandatory industrial-adjacent permits are municipal and civil-defense clearances for the physical showroom and warehouse premises.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable - no statutory industry operating permit for ISIC 4659 wholesale trade of used machinery; the Commercial Registration booklet and the municipal building-use approval (commercial use permit) constitute the operative authorization. If the company later adds maintenance works, an IDA Workshop License will be triggered.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA), Ministry of Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt (Category C - screening and registration only) under Ministerial Decree 710/2020 EIA lists: clean wholesale trading and warehousing of used machinery are not on the mandatory EIA list. If maintenance or washing is added at the yard, the project is re-graded to Category B (tailored registration with a simplified environmental consultation).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero process discharges in pure trading. For the machinery yard, the operator must maintain an impermeable surfaced floor, absorbent drip trays, and spill kits; waste oil, batteries, and hydraulic fluid must be transferred to EEAA-licensed hazardous waste contractors under Decree 274/2010. Wastewater from yard washing must meet Law 71/2017 and Decree 44/2000 discharge limits (BOD5 60 mg/L, COD 200 mg/L, TSS 60 mg/L, oil-and-grease 15 mg/L). Noise must not exceed 85 dB(A) at the workplace, and the ambient perimeter boundary must comply with Law 4/1994 maximums.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Mandatory Fire Safety Clearance from the Civil Defense Authority for any office and warehousing premises, requiring fire exits, extinguishers, emergency lighting, and separation of stored fuels. Municipal structural-load amenity certificate for any racking, display equipment, or lifting gear. Occupational health compliance under Decree 211/2015 for PPE, first aid kits, emergency preparedness, and a medical clearance record for yard personnel.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance; unified national tax administration and e-services portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg; electronic invoicing and receipt validation platforms operated by the ETA at https://invoicing.eta.gov.eg.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Egyptian LLC must first complete incorporation with the General Authority for Investment (GAFI) and the Commercial Registry (Ministry of Trade and Industry), then register with the ETA within the statutory registration period (before commencing activity or within 30 days of the start of operations) to obtain a unified Tax Card and VAT registration certificate. Procedure: (1) submit the commercial registration certificate, Articles of Association, lease or title deed, board resolution/power of attorney, and bank certificate through the ETA e-services portal or in person at the competent tax office; (2) receive the Tax Card and VAT certificate; (3) onboard to the ETA e-invoicing system through API registration and authentication; (4) register with the Customs Authority to obtain the exporter customs code used in export declarations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Egypt is a unitary civil-law jurisdiction and does not offer U.S.-style check-the-box elections or hybrid mismatch elections. An LLC is always treated as a separate taxable juridical person under Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005 and VAT Law No. 67 of 2016. Only limited statutory choices are available, such as cash-basis accounting for small taxpayers and the option to apply for VAT registration before the threshold is reached.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under Law No. 67 of 2016 as amended, together with its Executive Regulations; complementary stamp tax, customs duty, and excise regimes apply, but VAT governs the indirect tax treatment of trading activities.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 in annual taxable turnover under VAT Law No. 67 of 2016, Article 16. VAT registration is compulsory once actual annual turnover exceeds this threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory phased e-invoicing and e-receipt regimes apply to ETA-selected taxpayers. Issuers must integrate via ETA-approved APIs or the taxpayer portal, submit invoice data in real time, and obtain machine validation with a clearance decision (accepted or rejected). Each valid invoice bears a unique ETA scan code/QR element, and clearance is a legal precondition for input VAT deduction and for using the invoice in customs or export documentation. Non-integrated taxpayers are subject to administrative penalties and suspension of tax clearance certificates.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export of used construction excavators and machinery is zero-rated where the seller is VAT-registered, title passes to a non-resident customer, and the goods are physically exported from Egypt under a customs export declaration within the statutory export period. Deemed exports to qualified free zones and specified offshore services rendered to non-residents may also qualify. The taxpayer must maintain full documentary proof of export and must reconcile the export declaration with the ETA and Customs Authority records; input VAT attributable to export sales is creditable and refundable.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (Bayan) duly stamped by the Customs Authority and the ETA
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or CMR evidencing physical departure of the goods from Egypt
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) issued by an Egyptian bank, or SWIFT MT103/MT202 confirmation, evidencing receipt of export proceeds
Commercial invoice, sale contract, packing list, certificate of origin, and any valve/inspection records required for used heavy machinery
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ETA and Customs Authority conduct pre- and post-clearance audits and cross-check export declarations against bank remittance records. Fraudulent or unsupported zero-rating claims trigger reassessment of output VAT at 14%, late payment interest at approximately 1.25% per month, penalties under VAT Law No. 67 of 2016 Articles 61–65 ranging from fines equal to double the tax evaded to imprisonment for tax fraud, revocation of exporter and e-invoicing privileges, and retrospective clawback of input VAT refunds already paid, together with civil liability.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) - the sole monetary, banking, foreign exchange, and payment system regulator in Egypt, operating under Law No. 194 of 2020 (Central Banking and Monetary System Law) and the Banking Law No. 194 of 2020.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Egyptian Pound (EGP) is assessed as partially convertible with a liberalized current account and a regulated capital account. Current account transactions, including trade settlements, freight, insurance, and profit remittances, are generally permitted subject to documentary verification and CBE-established bank due diligence. Profit and dividend repatriation is legally feasible for non-resident shareholders of an Egyptian LLC provided that audited financial statements are filed, the corporate tax clearance certificate is current, and the remitting bank confirms that the underlying foreign exchange was acquired through a licensed Egyptian bank. Capital account operations (equity injections, shareholder loans, portfolio inflows, and external debt) require CBE registration, a licensed bank intermediary, and compliance with balance of payments balance-of-payments reporting codes. Following the 2022 and 2024 unified flexible exchange-rate reforms, prior import usance restrictions were largely dismantled, but large outbound transfers above CBE notification thresholds require supporting documentation and may be subject to the bank's enhanced due diligence and the national electronic foreign-currency declaration platform.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Egyptian exporters must repatriate foreign currency proceeds from export sales into a bank account held at an authorized CBE bank within statutory timeframes established by CBE Foreign Exchange Circulars and prevailing the prevailing trade finance directives. For used construction machinery and heavy equipment exports (ISIC 4659), the applicable repatriation window is typically 120 days from the date of the export bill of lading, with an expectation that the full invoice value is credited through the banking system. As of the most recent liberalization, the mandatory surrender-to-EGP ratio has been relaxed to effectively zero for most exporters, but exporters must maintain foreign currency receipts in registered accounts, complete the CBE export declaration form, and present supporting customs documentation (export customs declaration, commercial invoice, bill of lading, and packing list). Non-repatriation or late repatriation constitutes a CBE enforcement violation that can trigger bank account restrictions or administrative penalties; routes that route export proceeds directly to offshore accounts without CBE approval are prohibited.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility for offshore digital EMIs acting as the primary treasury rail. Egypt operates a closed banking regulatory perimeter under Law No. 194 of 2020 and CBE payment-service licensing rules; no non-bank foreign electronic money institution (EMI) may provide deposit-taking, payment-account, or foreign-exchange clearing services to an Egyptian LLC without a CBE license. Offshore EMIs such as Wise, Payoneer, or Revolut Business can serve only as auxiliary payout or receivable-concentration tools, and any onward transfer to an Egyptian bank account remains subject to CBE FX declaration and anti-money-laundering screening by the receiving bank. Consequently, the corporate onboarding blueprint relies exclusively on licensed Egyptian commercial banks for primary collections and settlement, with offshore EMI rails used solely for low-value contingency disbursements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively mandatory for corporate account opening. CBE anti-money-laundering regulations (Law No. 80 of 2002, as amended by Law No. 181 of 2022) and the unified AML/CFT rules require face-to-face identification for signatories, directors, and ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs). A remote-only or fully electronic onboarding process is not available for an Egyptian LLC with non-resident ownership; at least one authorized signatory or a duly appointed resident representative holding a notarized and legalized power of attorney must appear in person at the Egyptian bank branch. The bank may accept a video-call interview as supplementary evidence, but the physical KYC signature and identification check remain mandatory where the bank does not maintain a prior relationship with the UBOs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering red flags in used heavy-machinery transactions, including over- or under-invoicing, unexplained valuation gaps, or a cash-intensive transaction pattern.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent certified equipment appraisal or third-party machinery valuation report for each unit; original supplier commercial invoices; Egypt export/import customs declarations; bill of lading and packing list; proof of physical inspection (site inspection certificate or pre-shipment surveyor report); a sworn statement of the beneficial owners explaining the commercial rationale of the used-machinery margin; and transaction-level wiring documentation showing a traceable funds chain from the buyer's bank account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex or opaque beneficial-ownership structure involving non-resident shareholders, nominee directors, or a multi-jurisdiction holding chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and legalized (apostilled) certificate of incorporation and register of members for each entity in the ownership chain; the Egyptian LLC's constitutive contract (Aqd al-Ta'sis); a resolution of the board/shareholders designating authorized signatories; a complete UBO declaration with tax identification numbers; supporting CVs or professional references for directors; and a written narrative describing the commercial substance of the Egyptian entity's role in wholesale remarketing of secondhand excavators.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP, or adverse-media hits on counterparties, brokers, or customers in MENA or emerging markets where used excavators are redeployed.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A comprehensive sanctions and PEP screening report generated by the bank's compliance tooling; adverse-media search results with disposition details; CIP/KYC profiles for each major counterparty; end-user and end-use certificates for every underlying machine sale; transport and insurance documentation proving physical delivery to non-sanctioned jurisdictions; and a letter of undertaking from management that contract parties will not involve blocked goods or persons.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident shareholders intending to capitalize the Egyptian LLC must route the capital contribution via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 through a CBE-licensed correspondent bank into the LLC's foreign-currency account at an authorized Egyptian bank. The wire must quote the Egypt-balance-of-payments statistical purpose code: direct investment - equity capital. The receiving bank requires, in advance or alongside the wire, the LLC's valid commercial registry extract, the articles of association, a shareholders' resolution approving the capital injection amount and currency, the share-subscription instrument, and a source-of-funds statement from the remitting shareholder. The sending bank is required to include true and accurate originator and beneficiary details in compliance with FATF Recommendation 16; incomplete or ambiguous remittance data will cause CBE bank rejection. Inbound capital amounts above USD 100,000 trigger mandatory wire-level CBE electronic declaration and elevated enhanced due diligence, including confirmation that the foreign shareholder is not a PEP or sanctioned person; amounts exceeding USD 1 million may be deferred pending CBE balance-of-payments validation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for used construction excavators from international sellers are executed through (a) commercial letters of credit issued by the Egyptian bank via SWIFT MT700/MT740 series, with presentation of commercial invoice, insurance certificate, bill of lading, packing list, and independent inspection certificate as the preferred cleared rail for high-value sup-above USD 250,000 transactions; and (b) SWIFT MT103 direct wires for open-account balances and spare-part purchases, provided the buyer presents the customs import notification or a confirmed goods-arrival statement to the bank and quotes the correct balance-of-payments settlement code. For payments expected before the goods arrive, Egyptian banks require either a usance LC or a prior approval from the CBE's trade-finance unit, given residual documentary oversight for import payments above USD 20,000. All outbound disbursements must draw down from the LLC's EGP or foreign-currency account and cannot be made from a proceeds-surrender-exempt account without the corresponding underlying import documentation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable USD/EGP foreign-exchange forwards arranged bilaterally with an authorized Egyptian commercial bank under a signed ISDA- or local-market master agreement
CBE-approved cross-currency swap agreements designated as cash-flow hedges for confirmed foreign-currency receivables and payables arising from used-machinery purchase contracts

FX options (call or put) executed through CBE-licensed banks to hedge committed future import or export cash flows, subject to the real-economy underlying transaction test and CBE record-keeping requirements

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (CIT declaration) covering full fiscal-year taxable income
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) — Income Tax Directorate; submitted via the ETA e-portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after the close of the fiscal year; for a 31 December year-end, on or before 30 April of the following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly 'delayed tax' surcharge of 2% on unpaid tax, capped at 100% of assessed tax; administrative fine of EGP 5,000–50,000; enforced attachment of bank accounts and third-party receivables; in-absentia administrative assessment if the return remains unfiled; ETA clearance certificate withheld, blocking public tenders and import privileges.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Monthly VAT return for each tax period, including the twelfth-period closing return (annual VAT cycle closure)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) — VAT Directorate; e-tax filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly, no later than the last day of the month following the tax period; the twelfth-period return closes the annual cycle and is due by 31 January for a 31 December year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of EGP 5,000–100,000 per delayed monthly period; denial of input VAT credit offset for unfiled periods; automatic provisional assessment with an added margin; repeated non-filing triggers enforced collection and economic-court referral.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Commercial Registry renewal of the LLC's commercial registration (business name, activity code 4659, registered office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry Department, Ministry of Trade and Industry, or the GAFI one-stop shop for GAFI-registered LLCs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually between 1 January and 28 February of each calendar year, irrespective of the anniversary of initial incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Temporary suspension of commercial capacity; late fine of EGP 500–2,000; registration struck off administratively if renewal remains unpaid for 6 months, followed by deletion of the commercial file and forced reactivation procedures before any continuing trade.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO register confirmation certification (ultimate beneficial ownership confirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) electronic corporate portal; Financial Regulatory Authority AML supervision
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the ordinary general assembly, and in any event not later than 31 March following a 31 December year-end; any share transfer triggers a register update and GAFI notification within 15 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of EGP 10,000–100,000 under AML Law No. 80/2002 as amended; suspension of shareholder voting and dividend rights; rejection of registration of transferred membership interests; the register is subject to on-site inspection and freezing orders in non-compliance cases.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual social insurance wage declaration and final monthly contribution reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSI) — local branch of the registered office; electronic submission portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual wage declaration by 31 January of the following year; monthly contribution statements due by the 15th day of the month following the wage period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment surcharge of 2% for each month or fraction of a month on unpaid contributions, compounding up to 100% of the contribution; administrative fine of EGP 2,000–5,000 per unregistered employee; personal liability of the LLC manager for evaded amounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual audited financial statements, auditor's report, and ordinary general assembly approval minutes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Assembly of shareholders; filed with the ETA as an annex to the annual CIT return and archived in the GAFI/commercial registry corporate file
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Auditor appointment and audit completion ahead of the ordinary general assembly; assembly to approve the audited statements within 90 days of fiscal year-end; CIT annexation by 30 April
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Companies Law monetary penalties up to EGP 100,000; CIT return rejected as incomplete; ETA administrative estimation with an uplift where books are unaudited; dividend distributions legally ineffective without approved audited financial statements.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual transfer-pricing declaration and controlled-transaction disclosure (TP forms)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) — International Taxation Transfer Pricing Directorate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed concurrently with the annual CIT return; 30 April for a 31 December year-end; documentation files must be prepared no later than the return deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Primary tax adjustment under the arm's-length principle; possible uplift on adjusted amounts; administrative fine for late or defective disclosure; reversal of the burden of proof; cross-check coordinates with ETA review of related-party foreign payments.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory audit is compulsory for every Egyptian LLC without any capital- or revenue-based exemption. Companies Law No. 159/1981 requires each LLC to appoint at least one certified public accountant registered on the ETA's general list, and the auditor's report must be presented to the ordinary general assembly for approval of the financial statements. The ETA will not accept a CIT return as complete without the auditor's report; a dormant or inactive LLC must nonetheless maintain books and undergo a dissolution audit in order to be lawfully closed.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS) issued by Ministry of Finance Decree No. 666/2022, substantially converged with IFRS; statutory statements in EGP with permitted supplementary USD presentation for non-resident shareholders; IFRS-IASB standards apply directly only to banks, insurance undertakings, and listed entities under FRA/CBE supervision.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Companies Law amendment (Law No. 4/2022) and AML Law No. 80/2002, the LLC must file an annual confirmation of its UBO register with GAFI even when no ownership change has occurred. The confirmation is due within 30 days after the ordinary general assembly and no later than 31 March for a 31 December year-end. Any share transfer or any event moving a natural person's beneficial interest above the 10% or 25% threshold triggers a compulsory register update and GAFI notification within 15 days. The register must include the beneficial owner's full legal name, nationality, country of tax residence, exact percentage of direct/indirect ownership or control, and supporting identity documentation; it remains an on-site statutory book open to inspection by GAFI and FRA supervisors. Non-compliance suspends dividend distributions, blocks transfer registrations, and subjects the LLC and its officers to graduated fines up to EGP 100,000.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 – USD 1,500 per annum in Greater Cairo and the New Administrative Capital; USD 400 – USD 900 in regional governorates; typical service includes premises address, mail handling, and forwarding of statutory communications.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,200 – USD 2,500 for a certified Egyptian audit of a used-machinery wholesale LLC with annual revenues below USD 5 million; assumes EGP-denominated single-location books, no group consolidation, and no audit of related-party transfer-pricing files.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 22.5% flat CIT on net taxable income of resident LLCs (Law No. 26/2020, replacing the 20% rate under Law No. 91/2005); no ordinary local surtax for wholesale trading LLCs outside special economic zones.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SME preferential tax package (Law No. 71/2017 and ETA implementing decrees) allows small traders to elect a final tax on annual turnover rather than accounting profit, with graduated rates including 0% at the lowest band and fixed burdens for medium bands; the election is irrevocable and available only if turnover remains under statutory thresholds. Investment Law No. 72/2017 incentives (50% investment-cost deduction) are generally unavailable to pure wholesale resale projects because they are not in the priority sector list. Free-zone and SCZONE exemptions require real export-generating substance. Application of the 5-year loss carryforward remains the principal timing benefit for a heavy-machinery trading cycle.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: ETA Corporate Income Tax Return, Form No. 26, mandatorily e-filed on the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) electronic portal (https://www.eta.gov.eg), with audited financial statements, the TP Declaration, and e-invoice/e-receipt extracts attached electronically.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (plus two advance CIT installments within the tax year).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within four months after fiscal year-end (calendar-year filers: by 30 April). Advance installments of 25% each of the prior year's tax become payable at months 6 and 10 of the current tax year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total invoice value of used hydraulic excavators/rollers sold, including export sales, less returns and allowances per audited books.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident taxpayer with a PE, restrict to Egyptian-source sales; offshore title-passage sales are not Egyptian-source unless negotiated and executed through the PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Purchase price of secondhand machines, customs duties, marine/road freight, inspection, reconditioning, and direct handling costs allocated to units sold.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductible only when supported by customs import declarations and arm's-length invoices from the related supplier; related-party purchases require TP documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Warehousing, demurrage, site inspection, sales commission, director remuneration, financing costs, and allocated overheads of the remarketing activity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apportion under actual facts or an ETA-approved allocation key; head-office charges require TP documentation and Egyptian-source supporting evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income tax itself, unused provisions, entertainment exceeding statutory limits, costs without valid VAT/import invoices, and unpaid WHT on cross-border royalties, interest, or service fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add-back includes taxes borne on behalf of a non-resident where the contract was not grossed up in compliance with Egyptian law.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Previous-year tax losses claimed within the 5-year carryforward window, supported by a loss schedule prepared in accordance with ETA guidelines.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A PE may offset only its own Egyptian-source losses; parent-company losses are never attributed to the Egyptian branch.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final net taxable income multiplied by the 22.5% statutory rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The PE is taxed on attributable profit before repatriation; no deemed-remittance base applies at the CIT layer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance CIT installments paid during the year, foreign tax credits under DTA rules, and any prior-year overpayments credited by the ETA.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders cannot offset dividend distribution WHT against the LLC's CIT liability.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Settlement amount due to the ETA, or refund claim; refunds are subject to desk audit and statutory review periods.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any balance must be paid from the taxpayer's designated bank account; unpaid balances block export/inward remittance permissions and may trigger travel bans.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 5% per month (or part) of assessed tax; delay fine: 2% per month of unpaid tax under Law No. 2/2021; fixed non-filing fine of EGP 10,000–50,000; e-invoice non-compliance penalties of EGP 20,000–100,000 per transaction for large taxpayers.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: ETA Monthly Withholding Tax Return (Form No. 41), e-filed on the ETA portal; reports dividend distribution tax, non-resident royalty/interest/service WHT, and payroll-related withholdings.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: File and remit by the 15th day of the month following the calendar month in which the payment was made or the distribution was declared.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross dividends declared by the LLC to shareholders; 10% distribution WHT applies on the gross amount.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Treaty-reduced rate available only after ETA clearance and Tax Residency Certificate submission.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cross-border payments for IP licensing, know-how, and debt finance related to the machinery trading activity; statutory WHT of 20%.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach treaty relief schedules and beneficial-ownership declarations; treaty rates typically suspend to 10%–15%.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box C – Service and Contract Payments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cross-border commissions, agency fees, inspection services, and technical services connected to excavator remarketing.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: 20% WHT applies where services are performed or economically exploited in Egypt; pure offshore services may be treaty-exempt under business-profits articles.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to withhold and remit: full tax due, 2% per month delay fine, and 5% per month late-filing surcharge; repeated violations expose the file to escalation, bank-account attachment, and a ban on future dividend/remittance approvals.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% final dividend distribution WHT on the gross amount of profits distributed by the Egyptian LLC to shareholders, resident or non-resident alike (Law No. 91/2005, Art. 52; reaffirmed under Law No. 26/2020).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced DTA rate (dividends usually 5%–15%), the non-resident shareholder must: (1) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the home-country tax authority covering the payment year; (2) legalize the TRC through Egyptian consular attestation because Egypt is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention; (3) attach a certified Arabic translation; (4) submit the ETA Treaty Relief Application Form together with a beneficial-ownership declaration, shareholding/transfer records, and source-country financial statements; and (5) obtain prior written ETA confirmation. The Egyptian payer must retain the approved documentation for 10 years and disclose the treaty-rescued items on Form No. 41.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties and IP license fees: 20% statutory WHT; DTA floors commonly 10%–15%. Interest on non-resident loans and finance leases: 20% statutory WHT; treaty rates typically 10%–15%. Payments for secondhand machinery as goods carry no WHT, but any extended payment term, late-payment interest, or imbedded license/finance charge is separately recharacterized and exposed to the 20% WHT unless treaty relief is secured.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File mandatory where the aggregate value of related-party controlled transactions in a fiscal year exceeds EGP 5 million; Master File prepared where the multinational group's consolidated revenue exceeds EGP 750 million; a Transfer Pricing Disclosure Form must accompany Form No. 26 for any material related-party flow, regardless of size.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt has not enacted UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations; however, substance is enforced through the General Anti-Avoidance Rules (Law No. 91/2005, Arts. 30–33), the beneficial-ownership doctrine in DTA applications, and ETA audit practice requiring physical premises, personnel, bank accounts, real trade risk, and title-holding functions in the used-machinery merchant trade. Free-zone and SCZONE privileges lapse automatically where the entity fails to perform genuine inspection, freight, and inventory-resale functions from Egypt.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understating machinery resale revenue, using or issuing forged import invoices, splitting sales through shell dealers to remain under the SME turnover threshold, or destroying books before the statutory ten-year retention period.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Restoration of the full evaded tax plus a 40% penalty, escalated to 100% if forged documents are proven; criminal monetary penalties of EGP 50,000–5,000,000 and imprisonment up to five years under Law No. 2/2021.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for the full evaded amount where non-payment is caused by their willful default; the ETA may impose travel bans, attach personal bank accounts, and obtain criminal convictions leading to professional debarment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Egyptian LLC booking title and invoicing for used excavators while having no premises, no staff, no board meetings in Egypt, no local bank settlement of trade invoices, and actual sales management performed abroad.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of the entire net profit as a deemed distribution attracting the 10% WHT, disallowance of all cross-border expenses under GAAR, and revocation of commercial registration under Companies Law No. 72/2017 as a frustrated shell.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors signing knowingly false substance declarations face criminal exposure for tax evasion and money laundering; civil claw-back of management fees is available in insolvency proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting wire or Swift LC proceeds from sanctioned final users, handling cash-augmented sales not recorded in books, or routing payments through relatives' accounts without enhanced due diligence under Law No. 80/2002.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment for 3–15 years and fines up to EGP 5 million per AML violation; confiscation of excavators and transaction proceeds; asset-freeze orders can paralyze the LLC's banking lines pending review.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and ultimate beneficial owners are personally liable for financing illicit transactions; travel bans, asset freezes, and extradition under bilateral judicial assistance treaties may follow.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends to the foreign parent without depositing the 10% WHT; paying royalties or interest at gross with no 20% WHT and no treaty clearance; or wiring branch profit remittances without the applicable 5% remittance surtax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA re-assessment of the unpaid WHT plus 2% monthly delay fines and 5% late-filing surcharges; contractual gross-up clauses generate a second deemed-distribution tax layer; bank accounts and equipment receivables may be seized.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Unsatisfied WHT attaches permanently to the LLC's tax file; upon liquidation the ETA has priority claim, and directors who paid a dividend while taxes were due incur personal restitution obligations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Ignoring the EGP 5 million Local File threshold, submitting a TP declaration inconsistent with margins actually realized in related-party resale of used machinery, or refusing to disclose intercompany pricing arrangements with the offshore procurement arm.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Documentation fine of EGP 50,000–500,000; ETA adjustment to the full arm's-length margin with additional 22.5% CIT; the adjusted difference may be reclassified as a disguised dividend attracting a further 10% WHT, plus monthly delay fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A TP adjustment rendering the company insolvent exposes directors to liability for trading while insolvent; the ETA can collect the uncollected difference from board members under the executive collection law.
